title: Deferred-ack protocol and delivery safeguards for audit/residency events
creator: Asha Menon
description: Design and implement a deferred-ack delivery protocol + runtime safeguards for audit, retention, and residency events exported from Redwood. Goal is to provide guaranteed-at-least-once delivery semantics without overwhelming downstream subscribers, support residency-anchored delivery rules, and produce machine-readable evidence for audit trails.
background: Several recent customer audits and a postmortem highlighted two recurring problems: (1) spikes in evidence export load cause downstream webhook receivers to return transient 5xxs and time out, which cascades into retries that overload the event pipeline; (2) residency and retention assertions need a signed/verifiable handoff and must be stored with the correct region metadata before final ack. Current shipper acks on enqueue which provides weak guarantees for end-to-end delivery and leaves little room for backpressure management.
goals: Provide a deferred-ack handshake that only acknowledges events once residency and retention preconditions are durably recorded
Implement bounded retry/backoff and circuit-breaking to avoid cascading overload during receiver outages
Attach verifiable residency assertions and signing metadata to each delivered payload
Expose observable signals (per-route lag, retry rates, and drop counts) in Console for on-call and PMs
Preserve idempotency for consumers with a clear deduplication token contract
success_criteria: End-to-end evidence delivery SLO: 99.9% within 30 minutes for non-batch events under normal load
Retry storms reduced: peak retry concurrency to subscribers down by >= 70% in synthetic outage tests
Evidence payloads include residency-assertion and signed-proof headers in >= 99% of deliveries
Zero incidents caused by undelivered retention-delete-notices in the next quarter
implementation_plan: 1) Define wire contract: headers, idempotency token, residency-tag, signed-assertion format (JWS), and deferred-ack status codes. 2) Implement a delivery shim in the shipper that persists a 'delivery intent' record in regional ledger before attempting external delivery; only then returns success to upstream systems. 3) Add a delivery queue with backpressure-aware concurrency limits per-subscriber route and global circuit-breaker. 4) Implement deterministic dedupe using consumer-visible idempotency_token and server side dedupe window (configurable TTL). 5) Integrate KMS rotation & signing service and include a verification endpoint for auditors. 6) Add metrics/tracing and expose Console dashboards and incident runbooks.
phasing: Phase 1: Contract + small PoC (wire schema, JWS signing, per-route concurrency control)
Phase 2: Durable delivery-intent ledger + deferred ack server changes, limited rollout to low-risk partners
Phase 3: Autoscaling knobs and circuit-breaker tuning, full rollout, Console dashboards and runbook
Phase 4: Hardening: developer docs, security review, key-rotation automation, disaster recovery playbook
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc reviewed and approved by PM and Security (Confluence link in artifacts)
End-to-end PoC sends 10k events with simulated 50% receiver failure and demonstrates no retry storm
Observability: Grafana dashboard shows per-route queue depth, retry rate, last-success timestamp
Automated integration tests covering idempotency and signed-assertion verification
API docs and sample consumer verification client published
notes: Trade-offs: deferred-ack increases upstream latency and storage footprint (delivery-intent records). We mitigate via TTL compaction and per-tenant retention policies.
Consider an opt-in mode for partners that cannot verify signatures; fallback to unsigned but marked "unsigned" in header and routed to a lower-trust ingest path.
We should avoid changing existing webhook contract headers for older integrations; provide an opt-in new 'v2' header and route.
We will reuse existing KMS integration but need a short-lived signing token mechanism to minimize blast radius on key compromise. Ops to own rotation cadence.
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Kickoff w/ PM and Security. Agreed JWS (compact) for signed-assertion and 'X-RW-Residency' header format.
2026-03-12: PoC of signing flow complete (local KMS emulator). Basic delivery-intent ledger schema drafted; reviewed by infra team.
2026-03-12: Identified dependency on pubsub consumer checkpointing; opened follow-up ENG-83450 to add consumer visibility into dedupe window.
2026-03-13: Design review feedback: Security asks for encrypted payload-at-rest for delivery-intent ledger in non-US regions; added to acceptance criteria.
